question.text: Under the Income Tax Act as amended by the Finance Act 2005, exchange-traded derivative transactions are treated as:

answer.text: Non-speculative business income when carried out on a recognized stock exchange
Speculative income only if the trader is a registered stock broker
Speculative income unless the transaction value exceeds Rs. 1 crore
Speculative income unless the trader holds the position for at least 30 days

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the NISM Series VIII workbook (page 194), the Finance Act 2005 amended section 43(5) of the Income Tax Act to exclude derivative transactions carried out on a recognized stock exchange from the definition of speculative transactions, so such income is treated as non-speculative business income. The Trap: The cited passage does not impose a separate hedging-purpose condition, a minimum transaction value, a holding period, or a broker-registration requirement for the exclusion to apply. Note: Source: NISM Series VIII workbook, page 194.
